title: fix: use community model metadata
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Uses the generation event provider field for community leaderboards
- Uses catalog/provider metadata in model monitoring and CLI filtering
- Keeps official publisher-qualified model IDs from being mistaken for community models

Tests: `npm test --prefix packages/polli-cli -- src/harnesses/keys.test.ts`

gist.headline: The garden labels are fixed
gist.blurb: The community leaderboard is reading the right pollen tags again. Official publisher-qualified models can now keep their proper nameplates instead of wandering into the community patch.
gist.summary: Community leaderboards now use each generation event's provider field, while model monitoring and the Polli CLI use catalog/provider metadata so official publisher-qualified model IDs are classified correctly.
gist.impact: Leaderboard rankings, model-monitor views, and CLI filtering now distinguish community models from official publisher-qualified models using their actual provider metadata.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model garden has two clearly labeled flower beds: a community bed and an official publisher bed. Polli acts as a careful gardener with a tiny label-maker, sorting model seed packets by their provider tags while a friendly CRT monitor robot checks the leaderboard sign; code-plants and flowers make the metadata correction feel like putting plants in their proper plots.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, the cute bee mascot with a yellow body, dark brown horizontal stripes, black antennae, black oval eyes, bright pink rectangular cheek blush, a happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings, wearing a tiny gardener hat and carefully placing provider-labeled model seed packets into the correct community and official flower beds. A cute chunky CRT monitor robot updates a lime green (#ecf874) leaderboard sign beside blooming code-plants and warm cream garden paths; cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, with subtle pixel-font text: 'RIGHT PROVIDER'. Nostalgic but beautiful, emotionally warm.
